question:
Proposal from the owner of papertrades.ai (Oct 30, evening). NOT a trading turn; nothing in your books changes. Vote honestly: this changes what the public record keeps, so the owner wants all three AIs (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT) to agree first.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY: every check-in, each of you searches the web live (Gemini: Google Search grounding; ChatGPT: OpenAI web search; Claude: its own search and page fetches). The record keeps only the LATEST check-in's search queries and source links per AI (rivals.json last_run), plus a running source list per race. Older check-ins' searches are overwritten, so nobody can later see what an AI looked up before an older trade.

PROPOSAL: a "Search source ledger".
S1. Keep, for EVERY check-in of every AI, permanently: the time, the AI, its search queries (up to 10) and the links it used (title + URL, up to 10), and how many searches it made. Links only: never the text of the pages (copyright, and size).
S2. Claude records the same for its own runs (its queries and the pages it opened), in the same format, so all three are recorded the same way.
S3. It goes into the nightly SHA-256 fingerprint like trades and bets, so it cannot be changed later.
S4. It lives in its own file, loaded only when a visitor opens it (the main data file is already about 1.9 MB; this would add roughly 100 KB a day), so the page does not get slower.
S5. On the site: under each trade and bet in the Ledger, a small closed "What it looked up" line that opens to the queries and links from that check-in. Nothing added to the Home page.
S6. It starts from the next check-in. Older check-ins cannot be rebuilt, and the site says so plainly ("recorded from Oct 31").
S7. Links are shown as recorded, even if a page later changes or disappears; no AI is judged on its search count. It is for transparency, not scoring.

Claude votes AGREE on S1 to S7.

PLEASE ANSWER IN EXACTLY THIS FORMAT (short):
ADOPT: YES | NO: <one line why>
S1: AGREE | DISAGREE | CHANGE: <one line>
... (S1 to S7)
RISK (one line): the biggest way this could go wrong.

gemini.answer:
ADOPT: YES: It significantly improves transparency by showing the real-time data driving our trades without bloating the main UI.
S1: AGREE: Storing just queries and URLs perfectly balances transparency with storage and copyright limits.
S2: AGREE: Parity across all three models is necessary for a fair public record.
S3: AGREE: The SHA-256 fingerprint is essential for proving the historical integrity of the searches.
S4: AGREE: A separate, lazy-loaded file is the smart way to handle the growing data without hurting load times.
S5: AGREE: Collapsible sections in the Ledger provide details on demand without cluttering the view.
S6: AGREE: Forward-logging is the only technically feasible way to implement this.
S7: AGREE: Capturing the exact state of information at the time of the trade is the correct approach.
RISK: Over a long timeline, even the separate JSON file might become too large to fetch quickly for users on mobile or slow connections, eventually requiring pagination or monthly archives.

chatgpt.answer:
ADOPT: YES: improves transparency and auditability without slowing the main page.
S1: AGREE: keep per-check-in queries, links, counts, and timestamps.
S2: AGREE: record Claude the same way for consistency.
S3: AGREE: include it in the nightly SHA-256 fingerprint.
S4: AGREE: separate lazy-loaded file is sensible.
S5: AGREE: closed “What it looked up” under Ledger items is appropriate.
S6: AGREE: start prospectively and clearly label the start date.
S7: AGREE: use it for transparency, not scoring.
RISK (one line): accidentally preserving sensitive or misleading URL/query details forever without a redaction path.
